## TL;DR

Worktree cleanup now reclaims only what RepoOS can prove safe, and fails closed whenever lifecycle state is incomplete. I finished the third review finding: a merged, clean worktree whose branch has no matching task record is no longer removed, because a missing record cannot distinguish a completed task from a stale or partial index. The sweep, `repoos gc --dry-run`, and `repoos status` all report the same candidate/retained/external counts and reasons. `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` passes.

## Work and rationale

The review named three bugs. The first two — task-file content proof and rename accounting — were already addressed by the earlier self-check checkpoint: committed task files are compared byte-for-byte against main's canonical copy, and rename detection is disabled in both contribution comparisons so a rename is checked as an addition and a deletion. Those changes had tests, which I re-ran and kept.

The remaining gap was indeterminate lifecycle state. A feature worktree with no task record used to fall through to the content proof and be removed if its branch was merged or represented in main. That is unsafe: the index can legitimately be stale (a task file written a moment ago, a watcher update not yet applied) or partial (a malformed task file is skipped), so "no record" does not mean "no task". I added an explicit fail-closed gate that retains a live worktree with the reason "no task record for branch — lifecycle state unknown". Close-out candidates (`repoos/integrate/*`) are unaffected — they are throwaway by construction and remain guarded by the durable job store.

A vanished worktree directory is treated differently: there is no working tree left to protect, so only its branch ref can hold data. I kept the content proof for that case, which still reclaims stale merged metadata/branches but retains anything unmerged. This preserves the useful "half-deleted worktree" cleanup without letting an unknown task record pin dead metadata forever.

I also extracted the not-represented reason text into one helper so the normal and vanished-directory paths cannot drift. Docs in `docs/close-out-pipeline.md` now state that missing task records retain rather than reclaim, alongside the existing skip-on-unreadable-index/job-store rule.

## Approaches tried

I first considered making the sweep skip globally whenever any branch had no task record. That is too blunt: one stray branch would block all legitimate cleanup. Retaining just the unmatched worktree with an explicit reason gives the same safety with better operator visibility.

I also checked whether the server and close-out callers could pass an empty task list after a failed index build. The boot path now awaits the index and skips the sweep on rejection, and the core sweep already catches a thrown `buildIndex`. The durable close-out store is read independently of the caller's in-memory set and reports `known: false` on unreadable/malformed records, which skips cleanup entirely. With the missing-record gate, all three indeterminate-state routes are covered.

## Challenges and blockers

The reviewed line numbers referred to a commit before the last two self-check checkpoints, so two findings were already fixed. I verified them against the current code and tests rather than re-implementing. Running UI tests ad hoc initially failed because the Vue plugin only loads with `--config src/ui-app/vite.config.ts`; the same tests pass under the repository's normal test wrapper and under `repoos check`.

## Key learnings

Fail-closed cleanup needs a positive lifecycle proof, not just a content proof. Content says "main already has these bytes"; it does not say "nobody is using this worktree". A missing task record must therefore be a retention reason, and the only safe exception is a directory that no longer exists, where the branch ref is the sole data source.
